findingIndependentlyReproduced.title: getDefinition's term-lookup helper (findProvisionView) does not fully whitespace-normalize the queried term before comparing it to the stored OperativeProvisionView.definedTermRef, unlike its own SECTION-side comparison on the same line and unlike the fallback's resolveUniqueDefinitionByRef - a query term with irregular INTERNAL whitespace (a doubled space, a tab, a line-wrap) silently bypasses the FINDING-2/3 fix and re-triggers the ORIGINAL defect pattern (stale base-document text served as OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED, hiding a real, on-file CONFLICTED or non-ambiguity-PARTIAL amendment).

rootCauseTrace.1_howTermsAreStored: amendment/chain.ts's provisionKeyFor calls normalizeDefinedTermRef(effect.target.targetDefinedTermRef) = term.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().toLowerCase() - COLLAPSES all internal whitespace runs to a single space. buildProvisionView (operative-state.ts) stores this already-normalized value verbatim as OperativeProvisionView.definedTermRef.
rootCauseTrace.2_howGetDefinitionLooksItUp: semantic/tools.ts's findProvisionView (used by BOTH getOperativeProvision for sectionRef and getDefinition for term) compares definedTermRef with `(p.definedTermRef ?? '').toLowerCase() === ref.trim().toLowerCase()` - this ONLY trims leading/trailing whitespace and lowercases; it never collapses INTERNAL whitespace runs the way normalizeDefinedTermRef (or the SAME function's own SECTION-branch comparison two lines above it, which uses `.replace(/\s+/g, '')` on both sides) does.
rootCauseTrace.3_theGap: A query term whose internal whitespace does not exactly match the single-spaced canonical form (e.g. 'Consolidated  EBITDA' with a doubled space, or a tab/newline in place of a single space) fails findProvisionView's exact-string comparison even though it is unambiguously the SAME term. getDefinition then treats this as 'no recorded amendment activity for this term at all' and falls through to the no-recorded-amendment fallback branch.
rootCauseTrace.4_whyTheFallbackDoesNotFullyProtect: That fallback's own ambiguity check (resolveUniqueDefinitionByRef) DOES call normalizeDefinedTermRef on its query term internally, so it correctly re-catches the AMBIGUOUS-target-resolution class of uncertainty (2+ colliding physical definitions of the same term) even via a whitespace-mangled query - this is why Workstream B's own required 'multiple candidate definitions' scenario is NOT reopened by this finding. But resolveUniqueDefinitionByRef only asks 'how many PHYSICAL definitions does the base document have of this term' - it has no visibility into the SEPARATE axis of amendment-EFFECT-level uncertainty (two competing effects on the same, uniquely-resolved definition sharing one effective date -> OPERATIVE_STATE_CONFLICTED; or an applied effect that genuinely governs but supplied no capturable replacement text -> OPERATIVE_STATE_PARTIAL via textMissingDespiteAppliedEffect). For exactly those two states the base document's own physical definition IS unique, so the fallback reports UNIQUE, retrieves the raw StructuralIndex text via getDefinitionFullText, and returns it labeled OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED/source:base-document - textually indistinguishable from a term that was never amended at all, with zero disclosure of the real CONFLICTED/PARTIAL amendment on file. This is a verbatim recurrence of the exact defect class FINDING-2/3 was meant to close, reachable only because the fix's own required test (04's requiredEndToEndTest / testFileUpdates) always queries with the term's canonical, already-single-spaced form and never tried a whitespace-variant query.

findingIndependentlyReproduced.affectedStates: OPERATIVE_STATE_CONFLICTED (two amendment effects, same effective date, different text, single unique physical base definition) and OPERATIVE_STATE_PARTIAL-via-textMissingDespiteAppliedEffect (a real applied effect with no capturable newText) are both bypassable this way. OPERATIVE_STATE_PARTIAL-via-AMBIGUOUS/NOT_FOUND-target-resolution is NOT bypassable this way (the fallback's own resolveUniqueDefinitionByRef independently and correctly re-derives that verdict even from a whitespace-mangled query, since it normalizes internally) - confirmed as a genuine, working part of the fix by this audit's own positive-control test.
findingIndependentlyReproduced.notARegressionIntroducedByThisFix: findProvisionView itself was not touched by Workstream B's fix (it is a pre-existing, shared helper both getOperativeProvision and getDefinition already called before FINDING-2/3). The fix correctly closed the gate it targeted (operative?.currentText truthy-only gating) but did not audit/harden the term-matching helper the fix's own new code path depends on for its FIRST branch (operative ? ... : fallback) to even fire - the finding is a gap in the fix's OWN blast radius, not an unrelated pre-existing issue outside the fix's scope: it directly determines whether the fixed disclosure branch or the unfixed-equivalent fallback branch executes for a real query.

FINDING-2.claim: Workstream B claims getDefinition now discloses real operative status/unresolvedIssues in every branch where an OperativeProvisionView exists for the queried term.
FINDING-2.reason: The claim is true only when the queried term string exactly matches the OperativeProvisionView's own stored (whitespace-collapsed, lowercased) definedTermRef. A term queried with realistic irregular internal whitespace (doubled space, tab, line-wrap remnant - all plausible artifacts of an LLM tool-caller echoing a term name read from real, often OCR'd or line-wrapped contract text) is treated by getDefinition's own findProvisionView helper as having NO OperativeProvisionView at all, silently routing to the base-document fallback and re-serving stale, pre-amendment text labeled OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED/source:base-document, with the real on-file amendment status and unresolvedIssues completely undisclosed - the exact defect pattern FINDING-2 was meant to close.

reproductionEvidence.testCase: tests/certification/part-b-recert-finding2-3-independent.test.ts > 'FINDING-2/3 independent recertification - CONFLICTED definition (two same-date effects) + whitespace-variant query' > 'ADVERSARIAL (doubled internal space in the query term)'
reproductionEvidence.setup: Real base document defines "Consolidated EBITDA" = ... not to exceed $5,000,000 .... Two real AmendmentEffectCandidate rows, both targeting the SAME uniquely-resolved definition, both effective 2021-06-01 (identical date -> a genuine AMENDMENT_CONFLICT per chain.ts's own §22 rule), with different replacement texts ($9,000,000 and $12,000,000). computeOperativeContractState (real production code, unmocked) independently confirms provisions[0].status === 'OPERATIVE_STATE_CONFLICTED' and currentText === null.
reproductionEvidence.call: getDefinition tool's real .execute({ term: "Consolidated  EBITDA" }) (note: doubled space between the two words, otherwise identical to the term's own canonical spelling)
reproductionEvidence.actualResult: outcome.ok === true; result.status === 'OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED' (not CONFLICTED); result.text contains the stale '$5,000,000' figure; result.source === 'base-document'; result.text contains no mention of 'conflict' anywhere - the real, on-file CONFLICTED amendment (with two live $9,000,000/$12,000,000 candidates) is entirely undisclosed to the caller.
reproductionEvidence.controlConfirmingThisIsSpecificallyTheWh: The identical fixture queried with the exact canonical term "Consolidated EBITDA" (single space) correctly returns status OPERATIVE_STATE_CONFLICTED with the placeholder text and a 'conflict'-mentioning unresolvedIssues array - proving the fix's own core mechanism works correctly and this is specifically a term-matching (findProvisionView) gap, not a reversion of the CONFLICTED-detection logic itself.

FINDING-2.secondIndependentReproduction: The same bypass reproduces for OPERATIVE_STATE_PARTIAL via textMissingDespiteAppliedEffect (a real, applied, uniquely-resolved amendment effect with no capturable replacement text) using a TAB character inside the query term instead of a doubled space - see the same test file's second describe block. This confirms the gap is general to findProvisionView's own whitespace handling, not an artifact of one specific fixture.

FINDING-3.claim: Workstream B claims the specific unguarded pathway around cross-reference-audit.ts's ambiguous-DEFINITION-amendment protection - getDefinition silently serving an ambiguous DEFINITION amendment's stale text as settled fact - no longer exists.
FINDING-3.reason: FINDING-3 is framed by Workstream B's own doc as sharing FINDING-2's exact root cause and consequence: getDefinition (the LLM tool-calling surface) routing around cross-reference-audit.ts's own coverage-audit mechanism by serving a confident-looking answer through a DIFFERENT module than the one BLOCKER-6 actually hardens. The same reproduction above demonstrates that routing-around still occurs for a real, on-file amendment-level ambiguity (CONFLICTED - two amendment effects genuinely disputing what the term now means) whenever the query term carries incidental whitespace variation from the canonical stored form. This is not a claim that cross-reference-audit.ts's own mechanism (independently re-verified correct by Part A and untouched here) is itself broken - it is that getDefinition, the specific consuming surface FINDING-3 required to stop bypassing it, still can under this condition, exactly matching the finding's own stated shape ('the same getDefinition behavior bypasses otherwise-correct ambiguous-definition protection').
FINDING-3.reproductionEvidence: Same test evidence as FINDING-2 above (one root cause, shared per Workstream B's own framing in 04-definition-operative-safety-remediation.json §'oneRootCauseTwoConsequences') plus the dedicated divergence-check describe block ('getOperativeProvision's own whitespace discipline is NOT shared by getDefinition'), which builds twin CONFLICTED SECTION and DEFINITION fixtures from the identical amendment shape and shows getOperativeProvision(sectionRef: "6 . 01") correctly discloses OPERATIVE_STATE_CONFLICTED (its own findProvisionView comparison strips ALL whitespace) while getDefinition(term: "Consolidated  Net Income") on the twin DEFINITION fixture reports OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED and serves the stale $3,000,000 base figure - a direct, side-by-side demonstration that getOperativeProvision's already-correct discipline (the standard FINDING-2/3's fix was explicitly supposed to bring getDefinition up to) is not actually uniformly shared by getDefinition for this input class.

whatGenuinelyDoesWorkConfirmedByThisAudi: The core gating fix (operative ? disclose-status : fallback, replacing the old operative?.currentText-truthy-only gate) is real and correct: every test in this file that queries with the term's own exact canonical spelling gets the correct, honest disclosure for CONFLICTED, PARTIAL, and RESOLVED-after-a-chain-of-amendments states.

The 'multiple candidate definitions' (never-amended base-document collision) invariant genuinely holds even under this audit's own adversarial pressure and even (independently, via resolveUniqueDefinitionByRef's own internal normalization) survives a whitespace-mangled query term - this specific claimed behavior from 04's own doc is NOT falsified by this audit.

Chained/superseding amendments (3 sequential REPLACE_DEFINITION effects) are resolved to exactly the latest applied text and disclosed correctly via getDefinition when queried normally - no defect found in this scenario shape.

overallDisposition: STILL_OPEN for both FINDING-2 and FINDING-3 (one shared root cause, per Workstream B's own framing) - a concrete, reproducible, independently-authored adversarial test demonstrates that getDefinition's term-matching helper (findProvisionView in lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/tools.ts) does not fully whitespace-normalize the queried term before comparing it against the stored OperativeProvisionView.definedTermRef, unlike (a) its own SECTION-side sibling comparison two lines above it in the same function, (b) the normalizeDefinedTermRef normalization already applied when that definedTermRef was originally stored, and (c) the fallback path's own resolveUniqueDefinitionByRef. A query term with realistic irregular internal whitespace bypasses the entire FINDING-2/3 fix and re-triggers the original defect (stale text served as OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED, with a real on-file CONFLICTED or non-ambiguity-PARTIAL amendment left completely undisclosed) for exactly the two operative-state classes (CONFLICTED; PARTIAL-via-no-capturable-text) that are not independently re-caught by the fallback's own ambiguity check. Per this task's own constraints, no production code was modified to fix this - it is reported here as a concrete, reproducible finding for the responsible workstream (or a future remediation pass) to address, most directly by making findProvisionView's DEFINITION-branch comparison call the SAME normalizeDefinedTermRef (or an equivalent full-whitespace-collapse) primitive its own SECTION-branch neighbor and buildProvisionView already both use, rather than inventing a new normalization scheme.
recommendedFix_notApplied_forResponsible: In lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/tools.ts's findProvisionView, replace the DEFINITION-branch comparison `(p.definedTermRef ?? "").toLowerCase() === ref.trim().toLowerCase()` with a comparison against `normalizeDefinedTermRef(ref)` (import from amendment/chain.ts, already exported and already the exact function used to produce and store definedTermRef in the first place) - mirroring how the SECTION branch on the same line already fully normalizes both sides before comparing, and avoiding inventing a second, parallel normalization rule.
